title.narrative: IFES Bangladesh Election Support (BES) program 2025-2026 - Election support in Bangladesh IFES

description.narrative: Tillsammans International Foundation for Electoral Systems (IFES) genom programmet Bangladesh Election Support (BES) avser insatsen stärka kapacitet hos den nationella valmyndigheten att leverera fria, includerande och transparenta val. Även ökad kapacitet hos civilsamhället att avkräva ansvar för en transparent och demokratisk valprocess samt ökat medborgaransvar kopplat till val. Insatsen bedöms som relevant för den svenska strategin för Bangladesh och kommer att bidra till samtliga delmål inom stödområde 1 inom denna strategi: Mänskliga rättigheter, demokrati och rättsstatens principer samt jämställdhet. Mer konkret kommer insatsen att bidra till tre resultatområden; 1) Genom tekniskt stöd till Bangladesh valkommissionen etablera en oberoende and transparent valmyndighet, som genom strategisk kommunikation även kan motverka desinformation 2) Stärka kapacitet hos civilsamhällsorganisationer att nå ut till olika medborgargrupper, med fokus på marginaliserade grupper såsom urfolk, minoriteter, kvinnor från marginaliserade grupper samt förstagångsväljare - för medborgarutbildning, konfliktriskreducering samt öka valdeltagandet och 3) Utrusta kvinnor med ledarskapskompetens för ökat politiskt deltagande, med fokus på kvinnor boende i landsort och i socio-ekonomisk utsatthet, kvinnor med någon form av funktionsnedsättning samt etniska och religiösa minoriteter. Sveriges stöd ingår i en större programansats i samarbete med Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO), the EU Delegation in Bangladesh and Global Affairs Canada. Nära koordinering mellan samarbetspartners är inbyggd i programmet.

Together with the International Foundation for Electoral Systems (IFES) through the Bangladesh Election Support (BES) programme, the initiative aims to strengthen the capacity of the national electoral authority to deliver free, inclusive and transparent elections. Also increased capacity of civil society to demand responsibility for a transparent and democratic election process and increased civic responsibility linked to elections. The initiative is considered relevant to the Swedish strategy for Bangladesh and will contribute to all sub-goals within support area 1 within this strategy: Human rights, democracy and the rule of law and gender equality. More concretely, the initiative will contribute to three result areas; 1) Through technical assistance to the Bangladesh Election Commission, establish an independent and transparent electoral authority, which through strategic communication can also counter disinformation 2) Strengthen the capacity of civil society organisations to reach out to different civic groups, with a focus on marginalised groups such as indigenous peoples, minorities, women from marginalised groups and first-time voters - for civic education, conflict risk reduction and increasing voter turnout and 3) Equip women with leadership skills for increased political participation, with a focus on women living in rural areas and in socio-economic vulnerability, women with some form of disability, and ethnic and religious minorities. Sweden's support is part of a larger programme approach in collaboration with the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO), the EU Delegation in Bangladesh and Global Affairs Canada. Close coordination between partners is built into the program.

"Strenghthening Bangladesh´s Democratic Framework and Institutions: Bangladesh Elections Support (BES) program", has been developed by IFES based on key findings from a series of capacity assessments of the Bangladesh Election Commission, context analysis and assessments of the political landscape in which elections are to be held.
The program is comprised by three objectives/key areas of intervention:
1) Establishing the BEC as a more independent and accountable institution equipped with the capacity to deliver elections with integrity for all people.
2) Enhancing the capacity of civil society organizations, with special attention to those from historically marginalized groups, to deliver effective civic and voter education that fosters voter turnout and a lasting commitment to democratic culture and rights.
3) Equipping women, particularly rural women, women with disability, and ethnic- and religious minority women, with the skills to take on leadership roles and participate actively in the political process.
